title: Shift rule for derived functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories, $\mathcal A$ with enough injectives (for example $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]), and let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with right derived functor $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] computed on a bounded below complex $L$ by a K-injective resolution $L\to I(L)$ (a bounded below complex of injectives will do) as $RvL=v(I(L))$ [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ let

$$
 \sigma^n_L:\ Rv(L[n])\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(RvL)[n]
$$

be the shift isomorphism of $Rv$, i.e. the comparison of the two K-injective resolutions $L[n]\to I(L[n])$ and $L[n]\to I(L)[n]$ (for $n=1$ the isomorphism $\sigma$ making $Rv$ triangulated; for general $n$ its iterate), and for $M\in D(\mathcal B)$ and $k+a=a'$ let $\tau^{k,a}_M:\mathcal H^a(M[k])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^{a'}(M)$ be the canonical identification of the cohomology of a shifted complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an object $X$ of $\mathcal A$ write $X[-q]$ for the complex with $X$ in degree $q$ and $0$ elsewhere, which is the shift $(X[0])[-q]$ of $X$ placed in degree $0$.

Let $K\in\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)$ and $p,q\in\mathbf Z$. Then:

1. The composite

$$
 \mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[-q])\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \mathcal H^{p+q}(\sigma^{-q}_{\mathcal H^qK[0]})\ }\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[0])[-q]\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \tau^{-q,p+q}\ }\mathcal H^{p}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[0])\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$.
2. For $p\geq0$, composing it with the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal H^p(Rv(X[0]))\cong R^pv(X)$, $X=\mathcal H^qK$, where $R^pv$ is the right derived functor defined by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive], gives an isomorphism natural in $K$

$$
 \mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[-q])\bigr)\cong\mathcal H^{p}\bigl(Rv(\mathcal H^qK)\bigr)\cong R^pv(\mathcal H^qK).
$$

3. For $p<0$ all three objects are $0$.

proof.text: *The complex $\mathcal H^qK[-q]$.* Put $X=\mathcal H^q(K)$; $K\mapsto\mathcal H^q(K)$ is a functor $\operatorname{Ch}^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$. By the definition of the shift of a cochain complex, $(X[0])[-q]^i=(X[0])^{i-q}$, which is $X$ for $i=q$ and $0$ otherwise, with zero differential (the sign $(-1)^{-q}$ multiplies the zero map). So $\mathcal H^qK[-q]=(X[0])[-q]$ as complexes, equal on the nose and functorially in $K$; it is bounded below, so it lies in $D^+(\mathcal A)$ where $Rv$ is defined.

source.place: Homology, Definition 011G (definition-shift-cochain) and the remark after it: for an object $A$, $A[k]$ is $A$ in degree $-k$

proof.text: *The shift isomorphisms $\sigma^n$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], $Rv$ is a triangulated functor on $D^+$ with an isomorphism $\sigma_L:Rv(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RvL)[1]$, natural in $L$, given by comparing the K-injective resolutions $L[1]\to I(L[1])$ and $L[1]\to I(L)[1]$. Define $\sigma^0_L=\mathrm{id}$ and, for $n\geq0$, $\sigma^{n+1}_L$ as the composite $Rv(L[n+1])=Rv((L[n])[1])\xrightarrow{\sigma_{L[n]}}(Rv(L[n]))[1]\xrightarrow{\sigma^n_L[1]}(RvL)[n][1]=(RvL)[n+1]$; for $n>0$ define $\sigma^{-n}_L$ as the inverse of $\sigma^n_{L[-n]}[-n]:(Rv L)[-n]=(Rv((L[-n])[n]))[-n]\to(Rv(L[-n]))[n][-n]=Rv(L[-n])$. Composites, shifts and inverses of natural isomorphisms are natural isomorphisms, so every $\sigma^n_L$ is an isomorphism natural in $L$. (It is again the comparison of the K-injective resolutions $L[n]\to I(L[n])$ and $L[n]\to I(L)[n]$, by the uniqueness up to homotopy of such comparisons; this is the shift compatibility of derived functors, Stacks 05SU.) Take $L=X[0]$ and $n=-q$: $\sigma^{-q}_{X[0]}:Rv(X[-q])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv(X[0])[-q]$, natural in $X$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 05SU (lemma-derived-shift, line 4657): $RF(X)[n]=RF(X[n])$ canonically; Proposition 05SE (proposition-derived-functor, line 4895): $RF$ is an exact functor on its domain

proof.text: *Cohomology of the shift.* Apply [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] to $M=Rv(X[0])\in D^+(\mathcal B)$ with $k=-q$, $a=p+q$, $a'=k+a=p$: $\tau^{-q,p+q}_M:\mathcal H^{p+q}(M[-q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^{p}(M)$, natural in $M$, hence natural in $X$ after composing with the functor $X\mapsto Rv(X[0])$.

source.place: Homology, Definition 011H (definition-cohomology-shift); Derived Categories, Section 05RR (derived.tex line 3610): $H^i(K[n])=H^{i+n}(K)$

proof.text: *Part 1.* The composite of step 1's equality, $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ applied to $\sigma^{-q}_{X[0]}$ of step 2 (a functor carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms and natural transformations to natural transformations), and $\tau^{-q,p+q}$ of step 3 is the composite displayed in part 1. It is a composite of isomorphisms natural in $X$, hence an isomorphism natural in $X$, and, precomposing with the functor $K\mapsto X=\mathcal H^q(K)$, natural in $K$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 05SU and Section 05RR (line 3610); the composite is the one of the source repository's proof of `Functor.nonempty_grothendieckSpectralObject_H_iso` (WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/SpectralSequence/Grothendieck.lean, lines 186-203, isomorphisms e5 and e6)

proof.text: *Part 2.* For $p\geq0$, [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] gives the isomorphism $\theta^p_X:\mathcal H^p(Rv(X[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^pv(X)$, natural in $X$: an injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution of $X[0]$, so $Rv(X[0])\cong v(I^\bullet)$ and $\mathcal H^p(v(I^\bullet))$ is $R^pv(X)$ by [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Composing part 1 with $\theta^p_{\mathcal H^qK}$ gives the isomorphism of part 2; it is natural in $K$ because both factors are natural in $X$ and $X=\mathcal H^q(K)$ is functorial in $K$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Definition 015A (definition-higher-derived-functors), Lemma 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), Proposition 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics) (1), Lemma 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived)

proof.text: *Part 3.* Let $p<0$. The complex $X[0]$ has $\mathcal H^i(X[0])=0$ for $i<0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] (with $b=0$) gives $\mathcal H^p(Rv(X[0]))=0$; by part 1 also $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv(\mathcal H^qK[-q]))=0$. (Directly: $\mathcal H^i(X[-q])=0$ for $i<q$, and the same lemma with $b=q$ gives $\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rv(X[-q]))=0$ for $p+q<q$.) The middle term $\mathcal H^p(Rv(\mathcal H^qK))$ is the same object $\mathcal H^p(Rv(X[0]))$, so all three vanish; this is the convention $R^pv=0$ for $p<0$.

proof_origin.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 05SU (lemma-derived-shift), Definition 015A (definition-higher-derived-functors), Lemma 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing); Homology, Definitions 011G, 011H (homology.tex); the Stacks proof of 05SU is omitted and is written out in step 2

split_report.summary: Made the statement precise: hypotheses (A with enough injectives, e.g. Grothendieck; v left exact additive; Rv on D^+ via K-injective resolutions), the two '=' named as canonical isomorphisms (H^{p+q} of the shift isomorphism sigma^{-q} of Rv at H^qK[0], then the identification tau of the cohomology of a shifted object), naturality in K, the identification with R^pv for p>=0 only (R^pv of def-sp-left-exact-additive is defined for p>=0) and vanishing of all terms for p<0. Replaced the one-paragraph imported proof by six steps. Checked lem-sp-kinjective-computes: part (3) gives Rv(K[n]) ~ (RvK)[n] objectwise only (no naturality, not identified with the triangulated sigma), part (2) gives H^p(Rv(X[0])) ~ R^pv(X) objectwise only (no naturality) and both assume Grothendieck categories; it lies in unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite, which sk-thm-properbasechange does not cite. So the shift step now uses the closed tool node lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated (iterated to all n), the object identification uses the new node lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification (natural in X; Lean closed on slopmaster2: PlusSingle.lean), the cohomology of a shift the new Mathlib leaf lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift (Functor.ShiftSequence.shiftIso for DerivedCategory(.Plus).homologyFunctor), and p<0 the closed node lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing. Dropped def-sp-kinjective-bridge and lem-sp-kinjective-computes from the proof (def-sp-kinjective-bridge stays a statement dependency). The same chain of isomorphisms is written in Lean, sorry-free, inside the proof of Functor.nonempty_grothendieckSpectralObject_H_iso (slopmaster2, Grothendieck.lean 186-203), but not as a declaration of its own. Searched with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle and grep.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rightDerived_shift_identification [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (p q : ℤ) : let Hq := CochainComplex.Plus.ι C ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q let S := DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0 let RF := F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus let H := DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D 0 ∃ e : Hq ⋙ S ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory.Plus C) (-q) ⋙ RF ⋙ H.shift (p + q) ≅ Hq ⋙ S ⋙ RF ⋙ H.shift p, ∀ K : CochainComplex.Plus C, e.app K = (H.shift (p + q)).mapIso ((RF.commShiftIso (-q)).app (S.obj (Hq.obj K))) ≪≫ (H.shiftIso (-q) (p + q) p (by omega)).app (RF.obj (S.obj (Hq.obj K)))
